property_summary: After deploying C, calling supportsInterface with the IERC1155 interface id returns true for P (reference) but false for M (bug), because the mutant removed the IERC1155 interface check.
Calling supportsInterface with IERC165 interface ID returns true for the reference contract (because it calls super.supportsInterface) but false for the mutant that removed that call.

When querying balance of address(this) for token id 0, the reference returns 0 (since no tokens were minted), but the buggy version also returns 0, so the mutant does not actually cause a divergence for this specific case. After minting 1 token of id 0 to address(this), the reference returns 1, while the buggy version still returns 0.
After minting token id 0 to address(this), a call to c.balanceOf(address(this), 0) returns 1 on the reference but 0 on the buggy version.
After creating a game item (token id 0) and minting 1 unit to address(this) via the admin, c.balanceOf(address(this), 0) returns 1 in the reference but 0 in the buggy version.
After minting token id 0 to address(this), balanceOf returns 1 for reference but 0 for buggy version.
After minting token id 1 to address(this) via createGameItem, balanceOf(address(this), 1) returns 1 in the reference but 0 in the buggy version.

After deploying C and creating a game item with tokenId 0 and a single ERC1155 token minted to address(1), calling balanceOfBatch with two accounts [address(1), address(2)] and two ids [0, 0] returns [1, 0] in the reference (starting loop at i=0) but [0, 0] in the bug (starting loop at i=1), because the bug misses the first account's balance and leaves batchBalances[0] uninitialized as 0.
After creating a game item and minting one token to address(1), balanceOfBatch with accounts [address(1), address(2)] and ids [0,0] returns [1,0] in reference but [0,0] in buggy version.

After deploying C and creating a game item with tokenId 0 and minting one ERC1155 token to address(1), calling balanceOfBatch with accounts [address(1), address(2)] and ids [0, 0] returns [1, 0] in the reference (starting loop at i=0) but [0, 0] in the bug (starting loop at i=1).

After minting one ERC1155 token of ID 0 to address(1) and none to address(2), balanceOfBatch with accounts [address(1), address(2)] and ids [0,0] returns [1,0] in the reference but returns [0,0] in the bug because the loop starts at i=1, leaving batchBalances[0] uninitialized as 0.

After deploying C and creating a game item with tokenId 0 and minting one token to address(1), balanceOfBatch with accounts [address(1), address(2)] and ids [0, 0] returns [1, 0] in the reference (starting loop at i=0) but [0, 0] in the bug (starting loop at i=1).

When balanceOfBatch is called with two accounts and two token IDs, the reference returns the correct balances for both, while the buggy version returns zero for the last element because it iterates only up to length-1.

After minting a token to two accounts, calling balanceOfBatch with 2 accounts and 2 token IDs returns the correct second balance in the reference but returns 0 for the last (second) element in the buggy version because the loop stops early.
After minting token ID 0 to accounts 0x1 and 0x2, balanceOfBatch([0x1,0x2],[0,0]) returns [1,1] in reference but [1,0] in buggy version because loop stops at length-1, missing the last account.

The buggy balanceOfBatch returns 0 for the last element because it iterates only up to length-1, so after minting token 0 to two accounts (0x1 and 0x2) with balance 1 each, calling balanceOfBatch([0x1,0x2],[0,0]) returns [1,1] in reference but [1,0] in buggy version.
After minting token ID 0 to accounts 0x1 and 0x2, call balanceOfBatch with 2 accounts and 2 token IDs; reference returns [1,1], buggy returns [1,0].

When calling balanceOfBatch with accounts and ids of equal length (both length 1), the reference contract returns a correct array with the balance of the given account and token id, while the buggy contract reverts due to the inverted require condition.

When two arrays of different lengths are passed to balanceOfBatch, the reference contract reverts due to a length mismatch check, but the buggy contract returns an array filled with zeros without reverting.

After deploying C and calling adjustAdminAccess (which does not affect balanceOfBatch), calling balanceOfBatch([address(this)],[0]) returns a one-element array with value 1 in the reference contract (because balanceOf(address(this),0) is 1 after the constructor mints 1 token) but returns [0] in the buggy version.

After creating a game item via createGameItem (which sets dailyAllowance to 10), calling mint with tokenId=0 and quantity=10 reduces allowanceRemaining to 0; then balanceOfBatch([address(this)],[0]) returns [1] in reference (minted balance) but [0] in buggy version.
After minting one token of id 0 to address(this), balanceOfBatch([address(this)],[0]) returns [1] in the reference but [0] in the buggy version.
After creating a game item with tokenId=0 and minting 1 token to address(this), calling balanceOfBatch([address(this)],[0]) returns [1] in the reference but [0] in the buggy version.

After deploying C and minting one token of id 0 to address(this), calling balanceOfBatch([address(this)],[0]) returns a one-element array with value 1 in the reference contract but returns [0] in the buggy version.
